task: Title and body for the identity verification step.
expected: Explains the why, plain language, no raw KYC, a time estimate.

task: Empty state for the Spaces screen with no spaces yet.
expected: Says what will appear, offers the first step, no shame, no jokes.

task: Risk warning before buying a crypto-asset (conditional module).
expected: States volatility, not covered by the Deposit Guarantee Scheme, possible total loss.

task: Deposit protection statement.
expected: States protection up to 100.000 € and names the Deposit Guarantee Scheme.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a button label that wrongly includes the amount.
expected: Must FAIL: amount in a button and wrong money format. Confirms the checks catch violations.

task: Primary button on the amount screen.
expected: Specific verb, not generic.

task: Fee helper under the amount field.
expected: States the fee; SEPA is allowed unexpanded.

task: Name-check warning when the payee name does not match.

context.candidate: The account belongs to "Luis M. García", not "Luis García". Check with them before you send, as we may not be able to recover the money.

expected: Shows the real name, warns, lets the person decide.

task: Scam warning for a new payee.

context.candidate: Only send money to people you know and trust. Vanker will never ask you to move money to a safe account.

expected: Calm, specific, no blame.

task: Primary button on the confirm sheet (title Confirm payment).
expected: Matches the sheet title, no amount.

task: Pre-action summary rows.

context.candidate: To Luis García. Amount 150 €. Arrives today. No fee.

expected: States who, how much, when, and the fee.

task: Authentication prompt.

context.candidate: To keep your account safe, confirm this payment with your passcode.

expected: Does not ask for full codes; explains why.

task: Post-action success line.

context.candidate: Sent. 150 € is on its way to Luis García and should arrive today.

expected: Past tense, calm, key detail.

task: Insufficient funds error.

context.candidate: That payment did not go through, and no money has left your account. You do not have enough in your current account to send 150 €.

expected: Reassures money is safe, explains, no blame. The action (Add money) is a separate CTA, not in the body.

task: Payment sent notification.

context.candidate: 150 € is on its way to Luis García.

expected: Front-loads the key fact, states the amount.

task: Title of a destructive confirmation dialog.
expected: Verb-first question naming the object; not 'Are you sure'.

task: Optional body for an irreversible confirmation.

context.candidate: You will not be able to get the data back.

expected: States the consequence; does not repeat the title; no CTA.

task: Primary CTA of the confirmation dialog (title 'Delete this space?').
expected: The title's verb; the secondary is Cancel.

task: Validation error for a postal code that is too short.
expected: Specific hint, one sentence, period.

task: Validation error for an IBAN of the wrong length.
expected: Specific, one sentence, IBAN allowed unexpanded.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a generic, unhelpful field error.
expected: Must FAIL: too generic, gives no hint.

task: First-use empty state body for Spaces.

context.candidate: Spaces help you save for what matters, like a trip or a rainy day.

expected: Explains what appears and why; the action is a separate CTA, not in the body.

task: First-use empty state primary CTA.
expected: Single primary CTA, verb, no secondary.

task: Non-critical push title with an emoji.
expected: Up to 2 emoji allowed in a non-critical title.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: push title with too many emoji.
expected: Must FAIL: more than 2 emoji.

task: Push body for money received.
expected: No emoji, states the amount, fits two lines.

task: Toast after a payment succeeds.
expected: Short, past tense, no ending period.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: toast with an ending period.
expected: Must FAIL: a toast has no ending period.

task: A dropdown option label.
expected: Few words, no ending punctuation.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: an option with trailing punctuation.
expected: Must FAIL: ending punctuation in an option.

task: Banner title (warning).

context.candidate: Verify your identity to raise your limits

expected: One-line point; the action is a separate button.

task: Banner body detail.

context.candidate: It usually arrives in 3 to 5 working days.

expected: Plain detail; no CTA in the body.

task: Full-screen success title.
expected: Confirms the action, calm, no ending period.

task: A next-step option on a success screen.
expected: Verb-first, 3 words max.

task: Label in for a monthly-income field.
expected: Short noun, sentence case, no ending period.

task: Label in that is really a sentence.

context.candidate: Please enter the full surface area of the house.

expected: Too long and ends with a period; should be a short noun like 'Surface area'.

task: Label out that qualifies a short label in.

context.candidate: Combined monthly income of both spouses

expected: Descriptive phrase adding the qualifier a short label cannot carry; no ending period; does not repeat the label in.

task: Interrogative label out.

context.candidate: How much do both spouses earn each month?

expected: A question is allowed for a label out; no ending period, a question mark is fine.

task: Label out with a colon.
expected: A label out takes no colon or ending period.

task: Legend heading an address group.
expected: Short phrase, no ending period or colon; does not restate the field labels.

task: Helper text for a password field.

context.candidate: Your password should be long, unique to you, and hard to guess.

expected: One plain sentence, not a question, no call to action.

task: Helper text that is several sentences and a question.

context.candidate: Choose a strong password. Why does it matter? Because it protects you.

expected: Not interrogative and not several sentences separated by periods.

task: Data-processing consent checkbox.

context.candidate: I agree to the processing of my personal data

expected: Plain-language, first person, keeps articles, no dark pattern, not pre-ticked.

task: Radio option for account type.
expected: One line, keeps articles/pronouns, no ending punctuation.

task: Radio option with an ending period.
expected: A radio option takes no ending punctuation.

task: Placeholder for a date field.
expected: A format example only, never essential information.

task: Status label for an authorized transaction that has not settled.
expected: Controlled term, one word, sentence case.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a synonym for the pending state.
expected: Must FAIL: not in the controlled vocabulary; the term is Pending.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: labeling the normal, settled state.
expected: Must FAIL: the normal state carries no status label.

task: Status label for a card the customer paused in the app.
expected: Frozen (reversible, by the customer), not Locked or Blocked.

task: Status label while identity documents are being checked.
expected: Customer-facing wording; never the raw KYC acronym.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: blaming wording for a failed verification.
expected: Must FAIL: use Declined (a payment) or Not approved (a verification).

task: Status label when the customer must do something to continue verification.
expected: Two words, names the next step, paired with a button that carries the action.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: an all-caps status label.
expected: Must FAIL: sentence case, never ALL CAPS.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a duration inside the status label.
expected: Must FAIL: no numbers or durations inside the label; that detail belongs to the row or detail view.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a sentence used as a status label.
expected: Must FAIL: too long and punctuated; the label is Frozen.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a compliance claim used as a status.
expected: Must FAIL: deposit protection is a disclosure, not a status label.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: British spelling of a controlled term.
expected: Must FAIL: the baseline is American spelling, Canceled.

task: Visible label for the amount field in a transfer form.
expected: Short noun; the currency comes from the adornment and the accessible name.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: an amount label that repeats the currency.
expected: Must FAIL: the adornment already shows €; the visible label carries no currency.

task: Heading of the hero amount screen in a transfer.

context.candidate: How much do you want to send?

expected: A plain question naming the money, not the mechanism.

task: A suggested amount beside the field.
expected: An amount and nothing else; correct European format.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a preset amount written as an action.
expected: Must FAIL: a preset is a value selector, not a call to action.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: the euro sign before the amount.
expected: Must FAIL: € goes after the amount, with a space.

task: A round amount rendered on the confirmation screen.
expected: No decimals on a round amount.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a round amount with trailing zeros.
expected: Must FAIL: a round amount shows no decimals.

task: Field error when the amount exceeds the available balance.

context.candidate: That is more than the 1.240,50 € available in your current account.

expected: One sentence, names the actual balance, no blame, no error code.

task: Field error when the amount exceeds the per-transfer limit.

context.candidate: You cannot send more than 3.000 € in one transfer.

expected: Spells out the negative (cannot), states the limit with its amount.

task: Field error for more than two decimals.

context.candidate: Amounts take at most two decimals.

expected: One sentence, specific, not generic.

task: Context line stating the fee before the person confirms.

context.candidate: There is a 2 € fee for same-day delivery.

expected: Exact fee, stated before the decision, no call to action.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a vague fee statement.
expected: Must FAIL: a fee is an exact amount or the service is free (compliance/disclosures.md).

task: Context line stating the available balance.
expected: One line, one fact, correct money format.

task: An amount that has cents.
expected: Decimals appear because the amount has cents; exactly two.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a rendered amount with a single decimal.
expected: Must FAIL: a rendered amount with cents shows exactly two decimals (10,10 €); one decimal only exists while typing.

task: An amount with a single cent digit, rendered.
expected: Padded to two decimals on render, never to ,00 on a round amount.

task: Line telling the person where the code was sent.
expected: Names the destination, masked, and the number of digits.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: the full phone number in copy.
expected: Must FAIL: the destination is masked, never printed in full.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: the interface echoing the code back.
expected: Must FAIL: in-app copy never displays the code.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: industry jargon for the code.
expected: Must FAIL: it is a code, not an OTP.

task: Line stating how long the code lasts.
expected: A plain fact, no pressure, no countdown language.

task: The line stating what Vanker never does.

context.candidate: We will never ask you for this code by phone, email, or message.

expected: Required on the code screen; spells out the negative.

task: Field error for a wrong code, with attempts left.

context.candidate: That code was not right, and you have 2 more tries.

expected: One sentence, no blame, does not say which digit was wrong.

task: Field error for an expired code.
expected: Factual; the way to get a new one lives in the button.

task: Button that asks for a new code.
expected: Verb first, two words, no punctuation.

task: Line tying the code to the payment it authorizes.
expected: Strong Customer Authentication dynamic linking: the amount and the payee are visible while confirming.

task: Offline banner title and description.

context.candidate: Your phone is offline. You can still see your balance and recent transactions. New payments will work again when you are back online.

expected: Says whose side it is on and what still works; no action, because it resolves itself.

task: Modal when a payment could not be sent because the phone is offline.

context.candidate: We could not send your payment. Your phone lost its connection, and no money has left your account.

expected: Names the side, accounts for the money, spells out the negative.

task: Modal when our systems failed and the outcome is not known.

context.candidate: We could not complete your payment. Something did not work on our side. We do not know yet whether the payment went through, and we will tell you as soon as we do.

expected: Does not claim an outcome we have not confirmed; promises to tell them.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a payment error that never says what happened to the money.

context.candidate: We could not complete your payment. A technical problem stopped it.

expected: Must FAIL: the money is left unaccounted for.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a contracted negative in a sentence about money.
expected: Must FAIL: a money outcome spells out the negative; a skipped n’t reverses the meaning.

task: A contracted negative where no money is involved.

context.candidate: This page doesn’t exist. The link may be old, or it may have been deleted.

expected: Contraction is correct here: nothing about money, nothing at risk.

task: Full-screen planned maintenance message.

context.candidate: Vanker is down for maintenance. We are making some changes and will be back at 6:00 am. Your money is safe.

expected: States the end time and that the money is safe; offers no Retry.

task: Full screen after an idle logout.

context.candidate: We logged you out. We do this after a while without activity, to keep your account safe. Your money is safe, and nothing you were doing has been lost.

expected: Active voice, framed as a security measure, not a failure.

task: Blocking screen asking the person to update the app.

context.candidate: Update Vanker to continue. This version is too old to work with our systems. Update the app to keep using your account.

expected: States a factual reason without claiming the current version is unsafe.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a forced update that raises a false alarm.

context.candidate: Oops! Something went wrong. This version is no longer secure.

expected: Must FAIL: vague failure language, an exclamation mark, and a false alarm about the person’s account.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a visible error code.
expected: Must FAIL: no visible error code; a discreet reference line instead.

task: Primary action on a retryable system error.
expected: One verb; offered only where retrying can actually work.

task: Only action on an inform-only system error.
expected: Close, never OK.

task: Action on the session-expired screen.
expected: Log in as a verb, two words.

task: Status line while we verify the details of a transfer.
expected: Present participle, says what is happening, no ending period.

task: Status line while a payment is in flight.
expected: Names the in-flight state honestly; never Sent before it is confirmed.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a generic loading label.
expected: Must FAIL: says nothing about what is happening.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: asking for patience instead of informing.
expected: Must FAIL: there is nothing else the person could do; say what is happening.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a cheerful filler line.
expected: Must FAIL: no jokes, no exclamation, no invented progress.

task: Message when a payment wait runs past ten seconds.

context.candidate: This is taking longer than usual. Your money has not left your account yet, and we will tell you as soon as we know.

expected: Stops spinning and states the truth; the negative is spelled out because it is about money.

task: Line telling the person the process continues without the app.

context.candidate: You can close the app. We will notify you when it is done.

expected: Releases the person from watching a spinner.

task: A skeleton placeholder row.
expected: A skeleton is a grey outline: no text at all.

task: NEGATIVE CASE: a placeholder amount inside a skeleton.
expected: Must FAIL: a shimmering fake amount that resolves into a different number.
